## Merge-risk assessment

**high — Validate before merge. 🟠 Confidence: Medium.**

Assessed [head `d315f990540718aa83f6d629d56e9669df37b733`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/d315f990540718aa83f6d629d56e9669df37b733) against [base `ba31eabdb8f7c62489dfda66dc08c909bd451ed9`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/ba31eabdb8f7c62489dfda66dc08c909bd451ed9), with evidence cutoff **2026-11-23 21:27:16.784 UTC**.

The 31 additions are confined to `x86_64-8102_64h_o-r0`, but they are production platform enablement, not passive inventory. The [fast/warm/express reboot plugin](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/d315f990540718aa83f6d629d56e9669df37b733/platform/cisco/embedded/device/x86_64-8102_64h_o-r0/fast-reboot_plugin#L6-L34) unloads `leaba-q200`, writes reboot-mode scratch registers, and programs restart notifiers. Its [pinned caller](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/blob/51d152ea82c05b90e023b638f802fc6051c0f6a3/scripts/fast-reboot#L1258-L1376) invokes it after committing to service shutdown with fail-fast handling disabled. A failed or mismatched hardware operation can therefore carry incorrect state into reboot and require cold recovery. Generic watchdog arming exists, but does not establish this SKU's recovery contract. This device-level boot/forwarding exposure drives the category; missing tests alone do not.

[Build 1281579](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/runs/136152200554) and all **17/17 current check runs passed**. Its [tested merge](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/f9093519f18b778fba0d52c4944506b276bd70c6) contains the assessed head and base, and has the same tree as the head. However, the nine image jobs were **non-Cisco**, and runtime testing was skipped by the [existing platform-path selection rules](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/d315f990540718aa83f6d629d56e9669df37b733/.azure-pipelines/template-skipvstest.yml#L15-L25). These passes do not prove that the new device payload was packaged or exercised.

**Before merge:** provide a revision-pinned Cisco image/package manifest proving this directory and its shared plugins are installed; verify both HWSKU aliases and generated 64-port configuration, SAI/optics and sensor operation; demonstrate cold boot, supported fast/warm/express reboot, upgrade/rollback, and recovery from failed reboot preparation on the exact SKU. Confirm the firmware mappings and the external BSP/SDK revision used.

No confirmed candidate regression or added log-analyzer suppression was established. The complete public diff and revision-matched CI support the assessment, while unavailable BSP integration details and missing candidate hardware execution leave a credible compatibility/recovery alternative unresolved. This is advisory, not an approval or merge action.

MERGE_RISK=high

2. Correct or verify the `Ethernet184` lane map and run Cisco 8101 platform-specific build plus port/VOQ, SFP, PSU/fan, reboot, and boot/recovery checks across the new SKUs.

## Elastictest merge-risk assessment

**High merge risk — Changes required.** Confidence: High.

Assessed [head `25078574935c0999442c6de13b7e16f25e24d5f0`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/25078574935c0999442c6de13b7e16f25e24d5f0) against [base `94a5515916435d6989f1fd50e5cb66dee39fdac6`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/94a5515916435d6989f1fd50e5cb66dee39fdac6), with evidence cut off at `2026-11-23T03:29:20Z`.

- This changes production switch initialization and packet I/O: XGS moves from SAI 15.2.1/SDK 6.5.35 to early-access SAI 16.0/SDK 6.5.37, replaces the XGS kernel-module tree, changes KNET structure/limits, and adds LTSW HFT module loading. Failure paths include `syncd`/`orchagent` startup failure, dropped CPU-bound traffic, and unavailable ports.
- Exact-head [Azure build 1280756](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/be1b070f-be15-4154-aade-b1d3bfb17054/_build/results?buildId=1280756) tested [merge `7359e4f2…`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/7359e4f2fe85e49d769fa5df371e59bdbdbbdca2), which explicitly contains the assessed head and base. The Broadcom job built the XGS SAI and `opennsl-modules` packages plus XGS, DNX, and legacy-TH syncd images successfully.
- Hardware qualification is not current-head qualification. The broad t0/t1 run used [build 1274913](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/be1b070f-be15-4154-aade-b1d3bfb17054/_build/results?buildId=1274913), head `70683c7…`, and `saibcm-modules` `9e9c9c3…`; the later smoke used [build 1278466](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/be1b070f-be15-4154-aade-b1d3bfb17054/_build/results?buildId=1278466), head `8b135f2…`, and modules `7619a03…`. Current head `5ba4289…` additionally loads `linux_ngedk`/`linux_ngst` on LTSW chips, but no current-head physical run exercises that path.
- The candidate image reproducibly leaves PFC watchdog ineffective on affected Broadcom t1 SKUs: the main t1 qualification failed both PFC cases on both attempts; a second bed repeated both failures; a third bed ran all four PFC modules and all 16 logical PFC cases failed again on retry. The test log confirms storms were not detected and cleanup found a residual `PFC_WD|GLOBAL` configuration delta. This is tracked by [sonic-swss#5140](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/issues/5140); the proposed fix [sonic-buildimage#30896](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/30896) is still draft.
- Additional unclosed gaps are the acknowledged missing Condor3 ILT timer fix with no Condor3 coverage, and DNX/legacy-TH runtime compatibility: the shared `syncd` binary is built with the XGS SAI development package while those containers still ship older vendor libraries. Package/symbol checks and successful image builds do not replace boot and forwarding validation.
- Exact-head KVM CI is useful for generic integration but does not exercise Broadcom SAI or kernel modules. At the cutoff, 12 of 17 recorded plans finished and 5 failed; the t0-vpp lane had failed four separate attempts with differing signatures and another retry remained active.

**Required before merge:** land and validate the PFC watchdog fix (or an equivalent resolution), then run the exact current head on affected t1/dual-ToR Broadcom hardware; add current-head XGS plus LTSW/HFT and Condor3 boot/traffic coverage with log analysis enabled; and boot-test DNX and legacy-TH syncd against their shipped SAI libraries.

> Could you confirm whether removing "CPLD Watchdog" from WDT_IDENTITY creates a blocking compatibility issue for other Micas platforms?
> 
> This shared class is also packaged for products such as m2-w6510-48gt4v and m2-w6951-64hc-cp, whose configurations still load drivers registering that identity. Both initial discovery and _get_wdt() now accept only iTCO_wdt.
> 
> Our isolated base/head controls show that a CPLD-only backend is selected on base but rejected after this change, with arm() returning -1. No hardware test was performed.
> 
> Do those platforms have a supported alternative watchdog or a platform-specific implementation that avoids this path? If not, should CPLD support be retained and any FR4 iTCO preference scoped to that platform before merging?
> 
> AI-assisted review, reviewed by Ying Xie (@yxieca).

This change is not expected to introduce any compatibility issues for other Micas platforms.

The CPLD watchdog is designed to remain enabled during normal device operation and be disabled during a device reboot. This is opposite to the watchdog behavior currently used by SONiC, where the watchdog is enabled before a reboot and disabled after the system boots.

Therefore, we do not intend for `watchdogutil` to manage the CPLD watchdog. In fact, due to previous code issues, `watchdogutil` was already unable to control it correctly.

For this reason, removing `CPLD Watchdog` from `WDT_IDENTITY` is intentional. We should not retain CPLD watchdog support in this shared class, as it is not part of the intended `watchdogutil` management flow.

## End-to-end validation of `sonic-clear dhcp_server ipv4 lease`

### Environment
- **PR head:** `b4ed7d7b3`. Tested the CLI plugins, `dhcpservd`, `dhcp_lease`, `dhcp_cfggen` and the template. Files were md5-checked against the source.
- **Kea:** Debian-packaged `kea-dhcp4-server 2.6.3-1+deb13u1`.
  - Memfile: `/var/lib/kea/kea-lease.csv`
- **Other components:** SWSS, Redis State DB and `dhcp_relay` are the real containers.
- **Topology:** `Vlan1000` is in MATCH mode. Leases came from a real DORA through `dhcrelay` Option 82 on `Ethernet4`:
  - `MAIA-BMC` got `.21`
  - `MAIA-GPU` got `.22`
  - the unknown client got `.100`

### Results

| # | Scenario | Result |
|---|----------|--------|
| 1 | `sonic-clear dhcp_server ipv4 lease Vlan1000 192.168.0.22` | `rc=0`. When the CLI returned, `.22` was gone from Kea (`lease4-get-all`) and from State DB. `.21` and `.100` were kept. The memfile gained a deletion row (`valid_lifetime=0`), and `completed_id == request_id`. |
| 2 | Restart `kea-dhcp4` so it reloads the memfile | `.22` did not come back in Kea or State DB. |
| 3 | `... Vlan1000 --all` | `rc=0`. Kea and State DB were both empty when the CLI returned, with 3 deletion rows written. |
| 4 | `systemctl restart dhcp_server` (`dhcpservd` rebuilds from the lease file) | No leases came back. |
| 5 | Client re-runs DORA after clear, then a timed clear | The client got `.22` again and it showed in State DB. The clear succeeded. |
| 6 | State DB entry with no Kea lease | `dhcpservd` removed it after the signal-driven refresh. The CLI returned "No matching Kea lease" with `rc=1`. |
| 7 | No leases / both IP and `--all` / unknown VLAN | `rc=1` / `rc=2` usage error / `rc=1` "not configured". |

This PR is a huge bag of many different functionalities that should have been done in separate PRs.

1- MAC over fpm (bi-directional)
2- ZMQ NB
3- L2_NEXTHOP_GROUP over fpm
4- fpm ES_BACKUP msg removal (disagreeing with that)
5- reconcilation between FRRouting and SONiC
6- ES parameters config db (push from SONIC)

Also, FRRouting is missing a FSM per MAC evaluating its ownership.

Comments for each directional function must be clearly state. (FRR->SONIC or SONIC->FRR)

This work is highly confusing and will be very difficult to maintain / progress without proper cleanup.

[P1] FPM ownership is enabled too early
[fpm_apply_local_mac() sets fpm_owns_local_macs = true on the first received MAC](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/2f1487bd03bda97a452e1061e23ef87b785ec621/src/sonic-frr/dplane_fpm_sonic/dplane_fpm_sonic.c#L757-L770), while the replay-end handler correctly treats the marker as the ownership boundary. Once the first MAC arrives, the pre-kernel provider suppresses all subsequent local-MAC installs/deletes, including entries not yet replayed. A MAC added or removed during replay can therefore be missing or stale in the kernel FDB.
Keep ownership disabled until the replay marker, or track ownership per MAC.

[P1] Bridge-port deletes can target VlanX:unknown
[sonic_frr_redis_br_port_key()](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/2f1487bd03bda97a452e1061e23ef87b785ec621/src/sonic-frr/dplane_fpm_sonic/sonic_frr_redis_interface.c#L1165-L1178) reconstructs the interface name using if_lookup_by_index() and substitutes "unknown" when lookup fails. During interface/port teardown, the interface may already be gone when the queued delete is processed, so the code deletes Vlan100:unknown instead of the original key. The SHL/DF entries then remain stale in APP_DB.
Use the interface name already snapshot in the dataplane context rather than looking it up again.

[P2] PortChannel system_mac changes are not propagated
After an EVPN segment is configured, [self.es_cfg caches the generated commands](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/2f1487bd03bda97a452e1061e23ef87b785ec621/src/sonic-bgpcfgd/bgpcfgd/managers_evpn_mh.py#L90-L99). Later PORTCHANNEL updates only retry set_queue; already-configured segments are not reprocessed. Changing system_mac therefore leaves FRR using the old evpn mh es-sys-mac.
Reapply affected configured segments whenever their PortChannel dependency changes.

@tahmed-dev, one concern about dropping `EvpnMH` from the template. An EVPN-MH device that keeps the default `mac_sync_mode kernel` still needs `--kernel-mac-ext-learn`, and with this change it no longer gets it.

**Without the flag, MACs that an ES peer also advertises never age out.**
- zebra rewrites each such MAC in the kernel as its own static entry, with protocol zebra.
- From then on, zebra ignores every kernel event for that entry. The `RTPROT_ZEBRA` filter in `netlink_macfdb_change()` applies in every mode, not only in ext-learn mode.
- So when the host leaves and the entry is removed, zebra never hears about it. It keeps the MAC as local and keeps advertising it.
- When fdbsyncd writes with `proto hw`, its `bridge fdb del ... proto hw` doesn't match zebra's entry either. The protocol patch refuses a delete whose protocol differs from the entry's, so the entry also stays in the kernel.

Could the template keep the flag for MH devices in kernel mode? Either keep the `EvpnMH` subtype from the earlier revision, or enable the flag whenever the device has an `EVPN_ETHERNET_SEGMENT`.

**Separately, the hold-expiry change in 0129 is needed in kernel mode too.** In ext-learn mode with kernel sync:
- zebra flushes a still-active MAC when its peer-active hold timer expires.
- zebra's delete names protocol zebra, and the kernel refuses it for fdbsyncd's entry.
- The ASIC keeps refreshing the MAC, so fdbsyncd never reports it again.
- The host stays withdrawn until it has been quiet for longer than the FDB aging time.

Applying 0129's rule regardless of which module learns local MACs (flush only a local-inactive MAC at expiry) would fix both modes.

@bhouse-nexthop, thanks, both points are right.

On the hold expiry, I'll apply 0129's rule whenever zebra runs in ext-learn mode: at expiry it flushes only a local-inactive MAC. 0034 installs zebra's static entry only for an inactive MAC, so an active MAC's kernel entry is fdbsyncd's, and flushing it only withdraws a host the ASIC still has.

On the flag, there is a dependency. In ext-learn mode zebra tells its own kernel writes from fdbsyncd's by `NDA_PROTOCOL`, so kernel mode with the flag needs the kernel's FDB protocol patch, which sonic-net/sonic-linux-kernel#619 drops. Two ways out:
1. An EVPN-MH device syncs MACs over FPM, as an L3EvpnMH device already does: the template enables the flag whenever the device has an `EVPN_ETHERNET_SEGMENT`, and fdbsyncd and fpmsyncd treat such a device as fpm. Kernel mode stays for single-homed EVPN, and #619 can go in.
2. Kernel mode keeps working for EVPN-MH: the template enables the flag for a device with an Ethernet Segment in either mode, and the protocol patch stays.

I'd go with 1. Does that work for your deployments, or do you need kernel-mode EVPN-MH to stay?

2. **Remote MAC/IP neighbours are never installed.** With `--kernel-mac-ext-learn`, patch 0032 stops zebra from installing them, and FPM doesn't carry IP neighbours, so on an fpm device routing toward a host behind a remote VTEP has no neighbour and has to ARP for it. @tahmed-dev, following up on resync after the FPM connection drops. It turns out fpm mode needs it on any EVPN device, after a bgp restart too, so we wrote the module side.

First, the two points from my last comment. Now that 3bd7c8f adds pins on L2VNI VLANs, the ES-peer-synced MACs are covered, so we've dropped our module change for them. On local MACs nothing is missing after all: STATE_DB updates made while the connection is down queue up and reach zebra after the reconnect, and zebra keeps the MACs it already had.

**Remote MACs are not replayed on connect.** On a new connection the module replays LSPs, nexthop groups, routes, router MACs and pins (`fpm_rmac_send()` starts the pin replay, dplane_fpm_sonic.c:3991-4009). It does not replay the L2VNI remote MACs. So with both processes up, zebra's MAC writes during a drop are lost:
- a remote MAC zebra learns meanwhile never reaches APPL_DB, so its traffic floods;
- one it withdraws stays in APPL_DB and in the ASIC, pointing at the old VTEP, and never ages out.

A bgp restart ends the same way on the fpmsyncd side. MacSync takes over the existing rows (sonic-net/sonic-swss#4857, fpmsyncd/macsync.cpp:149-154) and removes a row only on zebra's per-MAC delete (:477-485). That delete never comes for a MAC withdrawn while bgp was down.

**Module change:** https://github.com/bhouse-nexthop/sonic-buildimage/commit/5f4fe12e67291e0cfff532f38bea3a1231a34fe1 (branch bhouse.fpm-mac-replay, on your head 7cf8ac6). After the router MACs, alongside the pin replay, the module walks every L2VNI's MAC table and sends each remote MAC the way `zebra_evpn_rem_mac_install()` writes it (FRR 10.7.1 zebra/zebra_evpn_mac.c:185-237):
- behind a remote ES, against the ES nexthop group, and skipped while that group is inactive;
- otherwise against the VTEP.

That includes a static local MAC zebra installs over the network port while its ES is down (`zebra_evpn_sync_mac_dp_install()`, zebra_evpn_mac.c:1456-1479). `fpm_mac_sent_remote()` now applies zebra's full test for that case (static MAC, active ES nexthop group), so a pin is dropped only when the remote write stands in for it.

A duplicate frozen by duplicate address detection is skipped, since zebra does not install it either (zebra_evpn_mac.c:2130-2137). A pin for a MAC zebra sends as remote is not written (`fpm_pin_superseded()`), so the remote write stands. When the output buffer is full, the walk resumes a second later, and `ZEBRA_MAC_FPM_SENT` marks what it has sent, as in the router MAC walk. The walk runs only in mac-ext-learn mode. The commit also makes `fpm_nl_enqueue()` refuse a message once `fpm_reconnect()` has closed the socket: a walk running on the main thread across a reconnect could otherwise add a write event on fd -1 and abort zebra on `assert(fd >= 0)` (lib/event.c:1335). The LSP and nexthop group walks then stop rather than retry at once while the socket is closed; the next connect restarts them.

fpmsyncd also has to withdraw the rows zebra does not send again after a restart. That part belongs to #4857, and we'll follow up there. It depends on this module change: without the replay, it would have nothing to tell a withdrawn MAC from one zebra still holds.

Tested on Broadcom TH5 and Q3D in fpm mode with EVPN-MH, after an FPM drop of a few minutes and after a bgp warm restart: MACs withdrawn meanwhile are removed from APPL_DB and the ASIC, and MACs added meanwhile are installed. Our EVPN and EVPN-MH suites pass in fpm mode on both, with bgp warm restart enabled and disabled. The two review fixes above (network-port MACs, the closed-socket check) came after those runs, so they are build- and unit-tested only: on your head, the module builds against FRR 10.7.1 with this repo's patch series with no new warnings, and fpm_mac_test passes.

One more gap, which is not specific to this PR: the module does not send the bridge port messages (DF, split horizon, ES backup nexthop group) again on connect either. That fix stands alone on master: sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#30432. It touches the same reconnect path, after the router MAC walk, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

@tahmed-dev, thanks for going through it. Short answers first: yes to a follow-up PR once #29312 merges, and yes to splitting out the `fpm_nl_enqueue()` check. Nothing here blocks #29312 from our side.

On the two fpmsyncd points. The fpmsyncd side is item 2 in my comment on sonic-net/sonic-swss#4857 (https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/pull/4857#issuecomment-6521502432, commit b52515478).

1. You're right, and it doesn't try to find the end of the replay. On every connect MacSync marks the remote rows stale, and it withdraws the ones zebra hasn't sent again only once zebra has sent at least one remote MAC and the FPM channel has then been quiet for 10 s, checked no earlier than 120 s after the connect, or at 600 s if no remote MAC comes at all (fpmsyncd/macsync.cpp:458-475 on bhouse.fpmsyncd-nhg-flush). The quiet window covers the whole channel, so a walk paused for a second or the separate pin walk can't set it off. The module commit message saying "once the replay is over" was loose; I'll fix it in the follow-up.

   An explicit end would only help the reconnect where zebra stays up: there the replay is everything zebra holds, so fpmsyncd could withdraw straight after it instead of waiting two minutes. If you'd like that, the module can send one marker after both the remote MAC walk and the pin walk have written their last message (both start in `fpm_rmac_send()`), with a flag saying whether this is zebra's first connect since it started, so fpmsyncd never acts on the near-empty replay after a restart. fpmsyncd skips FPM messages that aren't netlink (fpmsyncd/fpmlink.cpp:270), so a new FPM message type wouldn't upset an older fpmsyncd. I'd leave it out of the first follow-up.

2. It doesn't wait for BGP as such; it guesses with the timers above. That's the weak spot. If a peer's session comes up after the channel has settled, its MACs are withdrawn and then written again when zebra sends them, flooding in between. In a warm restart that costs exactly what warm restart is for.

   I agree the warm reconcile is the right point when warm restart is on. MacSync's stale rows can go there, next to `macsync.onWarmStartEnd()` (fpmsyncd.cpp:331-332). One catch: with bgp_eoiu set, the reconcile comes at the EOIU hold, and bgp_eoiu_marker.py only waits for the ipv4 and ipv6 unicast EORs (:53-57). So either the marker also waits for the l2vpn evpn EORs, or the MAC rows reconcile on the warm timer only, the way fdbsyncd reconciles them in kernel mode.

   With warm restart off there's no reconcile point at all, so after a cold bgp restart or an FPM drop the rows would stay for good. That case still needs a rule, and the settle rule is what's left there.

   So for the follow-up: reconcile at the warm restart point when warm restart is on, keep the settle rule only when it's off. I'll rework the #4857 commit that way.

On `fpm_nl_enqueue()`: agreed. I'll open the closed-socket check on its own against master, like #30432, and drop it from the replay commit.

@tahmed-dev, on the `fpm_nl_enqueue()` split: before opening it I went back over the race, and master doesn't have it. `fpm_reconnect()` cancels every walk with `event_cancel_async()`, which waits until the main thread has processed the cancel, so no walk is running or queued when the socket closes, and the dplane path already checks the socket. The same holds on #29312's head, where the pin and remote MAC walks are in that cancel list too. So there's nothing to backport, and I'll leave the check out of the replay follow-up as well.
